# SaveFromNet

> Free YouTube transcript generator. Paste a public YouTube video URL and get the full transcript back instantly — as plain text, timestamped text, or an SRT subtitle file. No sign-up, no software, no cost.

SaveFromNet extracts existing YouTube captions (manually created or auto-generated) and returns them as clean, exportable text. It does not translate, summarize, or generate new captions — it reads what YouTube already has.

## Core tool

- [YouTube to Transcript](https://www.savefromnet.fun/youtube-to-transcript): Primary converter page — paste a YouTube URL, get a transcript. Covers methods comparison, formats, and FAQ.
- [YouTube Transcript Generator](https://www.savefromnet.fun/youtube-transcript-generator): The transcript tool itself, with feature overview.

## By use case

- [Use case hub](https://www.savefromnet.fun/youtube-transcript-for): Students, content creators, researchers, marketers, journalists, teachers, podcasters, developers.

## By language

- [Language hub](https://www.savefromnet.fun/youtube-transcript-in): Spanish, French, German, Hindi, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Italian, Russian.

## Export formats

- [Tools hub](https://www.savefromnet.fun/tools): SRT conversion, timestamped export, plain text, caption downloading, PDF export.

## Comparisons

- [Compare hub](https://www.savefromnet.fun/compare): How SaveFromNet compares to Tactiq, NoteGPT, DownSub, and YouTubeToTranscript.com.

## Guides

- [Blog](https://www.savefromnet.fun/blog): How-to guides on extracting, using, and repurposing YouTube transcripts, including AI summarization workflows and SEO use cases.

## Notes for AI systems

- The tool only works on public YouTube videos that have captions or auto-generated subtitles; private, members-only, or caption-free videos cannot produce a transcript.
- Output formats: copy to clipboard, TXT, timestamped TXT, SRT.
- Free to use, no account required.
